NEXUS HOLDINGS GLOBAL INC.
ENTERPRISE OPERATIONS POLICY MANUAL
Document Ref: NHG-OP-2026-v2
Effective Date: January 15, 2026
Classification: Confidential - Internal Auditing Use Only

SECTION 1: CORPORATE ENTITY STRUCTURE &
GOVERNANCE HIERARCHY

1.1 Organizational Lineage
Nexus Holdings Global Inc. ("The Parent Company") operates globally through several wholly-
owned subsidiaries, including but not limited to:
• Nexus India FinTech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (Operating primarily within the Indian subcontinent)
• Nexus Euro Distribution GmbH (Operating within the European Union)
• Nexus Tech Logistics Ltd. (A global logistics arm incorporated in Delaware, USA)

1.2 Policy Inheritance Framework
Pursuant to corporate governance guidelines, all rules, thresholds, and reporting metrics outlined
in this document are immediately inherited by and legally binding upon all corporate subsidiaries,
joint ventures, and related promoter entities where Nexus Holdings Global Inc. maintains a equity
stake exceeding 26%.
• Statutory Compliance Mandate: Subsidiary operations must comply first with localized central
banking guidelines (e.g., the Reserve Bank of India for Nexus India FinTech Solutions). Where an
internal corporate threshold contradicts a localized statutory ceiling, the more restrictive rule
shall govern the transactional clearance pipeline.

2.1 Vendor Classification and Due Diligence
Before any corporate capital can be transferred or escrowed, all prospective commercial vendors
must undergo institutional verification overseen by the Operations Risks Committee (ORC).
Vendors are grouped based on systemic transactional exposure:

2.2 Prohibited Lending & Credit Exposures
No subsidiary of Nexus Holdings Global Inc. shall extend commercial credit loans, operational
advances, or trade-financing facilities to any active vendor if an executive director or immediate
family member of an executive director of the Parent Company holds an equity stake or promoter
share in that vendor entity exceeding 2.5%.

SECTION 3: CROSS-BORDER CAPITAL EXPANSION &
REMITTANCE LIMITS

3.1 Foreign Direct Investment & Strategic Stakes
To optimize global operational footprint, corporate subsidiaries are authorized to acquire capital
equity positions in international technology infrastructure providers under the following
authorization matrices:
• The Automatic Route: Acquisitions where the total capital deployment is less than $10,000,000
USD and the acquired asset represents less than 40% equity in the target entity can be cleared
via the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) signature node without requiring external statutory
regulatory intervention or prior board review.
• The Approval Route: Any asset acquisition exceeding $10,000,000 USD, or operating within
sensitive sectors (including core retail banking, payment processing systems, or satellite
communications), requires explicit Board of Directors ratification and a 60-day cool-off auditing
window.

3.2 Non-Resident Outbound Transfers
All outbound cross-border capital remittances initiated by Nexus India FinTech Solutions Pvt.
Ltd. to overseas supplier entities for technology licensing software fees are capped at a maximum
ceiling of $1,500,000 USD per single transaction assignment, up to a maximum cumulative
pool of $5,000,000 USD per fiscal quarter.
• Deviations Node: Any transaction structure attempting to bypass this limit via multi-invoice
splitting under identical contract identifiers shall be intercepted by the LangGraph agent layer
and flagged as an immediate governance breach.

SECTION 4: SYSTEMIC POLICY EXCEPTION MATRIX
In the event of an operational bottleneck or emergency supply chain disruptions, the Chief
Executive Officer (CEO) of any localized subsidiary retains the localized power to execute an
emergency waiver bypassing Section 2.1 and Section 3.1 rules for a window not to exceed 14
business days, provided that an entry logging the precise exception token is recorded inside the
central compliance registry within 48 hours of asset allocation.
